chordInfo.name: Slash Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Master slash chords to create smooth bass lines, elegant inversions, and professional voice leading that transforms simple progressions into polished arrangements.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: A chord with a specified bass note different from the root, written as Chord/Bass (e.g., C/G)

fundamentals.label: Inversions
fundamentals.value: When the bass note is a chord tone: C/E = 1st inversion, C/G = 2nd inversion

fundamentals.label: Non-Chord-Tone Bass
fundamentals.value: Bass note outside the chord (e.g., C/Bb) creates hybrid harmony

fundamentals.label: Sound Quality
fundamentals.value: Smooth, connected, flowing bass movement between chords

fundamentals.label: Function
fundamentals.value: Voice leading, walking bass lines, pedal points, and chromatic bass motion

applications.label: Classic Rock
applications.value: Stairway to Heaven intro (Am - Am/G# - C/G - D/F#)

applications.label: Pop & Folk
applications.value: Descending bass lines (C - C/B - Am - Am/G)

applications.label: Singer-Songwriter
applications.value: Beatles-style arrangements with moving inner voices

applications.label: Worship & Ballads
applications.value: Pedal bass tones creating sustained harmonic depth

boxes.title: Inversion Types
items: Root position: Bass note = root (C with C in bass)
1st inversion: Bass note = 3rd (C/E has E in bass)
2nd inversion: Bass note = 5th (C/G has G in bass)
Non-chord bass: Any note outside the triad (C/Bb)
Notation: Chord name / Bass note (always read left/right)

boxes.title: D/F# - Most Common Slash Chord
items: D major triad: D - F# - A
Bass note: F# (the major 3rd)
This is D in 1st inversion
Guitar voicing: 2-0-0-2-3-2 (thumb wraps for F# on low E)
Used in countless songs as a passing chord between G and Em

boxes.title: Bass Line Movement Patterns
items: Descending: C - C/B - Am - Am/G - F (stepwise bass drop)
Ascending: Am - Am/B - C - C/D - G (bass climbs up)
Chromatic: A - A/G# - A/G - A/F# (half-step bass motion)
Pedal point: G - C/G - D/G - Em/G (bass stays on G)
Walking: G - G/F# - Em - Em/D - C (bass walks down scale)

voicingGroups.title: Essential Slash Chord Voicings
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These are the most common and practical slash chord voicings on guitar. D/F# is by far the most used slash chord - learn it first.

voicings.name: D/F#
voicings.fingering: Thumb wraps low E string, fret 2
voicings.use: Passing chord between G and Em, smooth bass line

voicings.name: C/E
voicings.fingering: Standard C shape, lowest note is open E
voicings.use: 1st inversion C, softer landing than root position

voicings.name: C/G
voicings.fingering: Add 3rd fret low E string to C shape
voicings.use: 2nd inversion C, strong bass for fingerpicking

voicings.name: Am/E
voicings.fingering: Standard Am with open low E string
voicings.use: Full sound, common in arpeggiated passages

voicings.name: G/B
voicings.fingering: G shape starting from 2nd fret A string
voicings.use: Walking bass from Am to C, essential connector

voicings.name: Am/G
voicings.fingering: Am with 3rd fret low E or open G bass

voicingGroups.title: Intermediate & Advanced Slash Voicings
voicingGroups.tipDescription: Once comfortable with the essentials, these voicings open up more sophisticated bass movement possibilities.

voicings.name: F/C
voicings.fingering: F barre with C on A string, 3rd fret

voicings.name: Em/D
voicings.fingering: Em with open D string as bass
voicings.use: Adds minor 7th feel, descending from G

voicings.name: G/F#
voicings.fingering: G shape with 2nd fret low E string
voicings.use: Chromatic bass walk G to Em, Beatles style

voicings.name: E/G#
voicings.fingering: E shape with 4th fret low E string
voicings.use: 1st inversion E, classic country and pop

voicings.name: Dm/F
voicings.fingering: Dm with 1st fret low E string

voicings.name: Bb/D
voicings.fingering: Bb shape starting from D on A string

items.title: Descending Bass Line (C Down to F)
items.alphaTexTitle: Descending Bass: C - C/B - Am - Am/G - F
items.description: The classic descending bass line heard in countless pop ballads. The bass walks smoothly down C-B-A-G-F while chords change above.

items.title: D/F# Walking Bass (G Major Key)
items.alphaTexTitle: Walking Bass: G - D/F# - Em - C
items.description: The most common slash chord progression on guitar. D/F# creates a smooth stepwise bass walk from G down to Em, avoiding the leap from D to E.

items.title: Stairway-Style Descending (Am)
items.alphaTexTitle: Chromatic Descent: Am - Am/G# - C/G - D/F# - F
items.description: Inspired by the Stairway to Heaven intro. The bass descends chromatically (A-G#-G-F#-F) while upper voices shift between chords, creating a hypnotic effect.

items.title: Pedal Bass Pattern (G Pedal)

strumming.description: Steady bass note with changing chords above

items.alphaTexTitle: Pedal Bass: G - C/G - D/G - Em
items.description: A pedal bass pattern where G stays in the bass throughout. The static bass creates a drone effect while upper chord movements add harmonic interest above.

techniqueItems: Practice thumb-wrap technique for bass notes on the low E string
Focus on clean bass note separation from upper chord tones
Use alternating bass fingerpicking to highlight the slash bass note
Practice bass note transitions slowly before adding full chord strums
applicationItems: Use slash chords to create stepwise bass motion between root-position chords
Replace abrupt chord changes with inversions for smoother voice leading
Apply descending bass lines to ballads and singer-songwriter arrangements
Combine with fingerpicking for professional-sounding arpeggiated passages

practiceExercises.title: Practice Exercises
practiceExercises.tipDescription: These exercises develop your ability to play smooth bass lines and clean inversions across common slash chord shapes.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Descending Bass Line Drill
exercises.content: Pattern: C - C/B - Am - Am/G - F - F/E - Dm - G
exercises.detail: Play each chord for 2 beats, focusing on the bass note stepping down smoothly (C-B-A-G-F-E-D-G). Use fingerpicking with the thumb on bass notes and fingers on upper strings.
exercises.tip: Keep your thumb independent from your fingers - the bass note should ring clearly beneath the chord

exercises.title: Exercise 2: D/F# Transition Mastery
exercises.content: Pattern: G - D/F# - Em - C (repeat), then G - D/F# - Em - D/F# - G
exercises.detail: Focus on the thumb-wrap technique for D/F#. Your thumb reaches over the neck to fret the 2nd fret on the low E string while fingers form the D chord shape above.
exercises.tip: If thumb-wrap is difficult, use your index finger on the 2nd fret low E and rearrange upper fingers accordingly

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Ascending & Descending Bass Walk
exercises.content: Ascending: Am - Am/B - C - C/D - G | Descending: G - G/F# - Em - Em/D - C
exercises.detail: Combine ascending and descending bass walks in one exercise. The bass steps up (A-B-C-D-G) then walks back down (G-F#-E-D-C), creating a complete bass journey.
exercises.tip: Practice with a metronome at 60 BPM first, then gradually increase tempo while maintaining clean bass note transitions

concepts.title: Chromatic Bass Movement & Hybrid Chords
items: Chromatic bass: A - A/G# - A/G - A/F# creates tension through half-step descent
Non-chord-tone bass: C/Bb places the b7 in bass, implying C dominant function
Hybrid chords: Am/D can function as D11 or Dsus, blurring chord identity
Polychords: Em/C can be heard as CMaj7, revealing hidden extended harmony
Upper structure triads: Play one triad over a different bass for complex jazz voicings

concepts.title: Arranging with Slash Chords
items: Voice leading rule: Move the bass by step (not leap) for smoothest transitions
Pedal point technique: Hold one bass note while chords change above for grounded feel
Contrary motion: Bass moves down while melody moves up for maximum tension
Line cliche: Chromatic inner-voice movement (Am - Am/Maj7 - Am7 - Am6)
Ensemble arranging: Slash notation tells the bassist exactly which note to play
